html:
Overview

Iona Sophia Jessica is the only daughter of Duke Desmond Origin and Lady Sophia Jessica, sister of Richard and Erwin. (Sophia Jessica Augusta) At court and among the people, her name is the Northern Princess. She studied in the boarding house of Elena-u-Lake and lived there in the same room with Alanis Almera for four years. (Elena-by-the-Lake Boarding School) Beginning with the novel A Doll on the Throne, some of the chapters are told on her behalf; they are called The Northern Bird.

Iona was born on March 17; year of birth is not named. She herself said that she was born in the tower above the arsenal of the First Winter. In the castle of the First Winter, according to local legend, a child born within the walls can be cursed: the ghosts of people killed by the Origins enter the baby, so the maids go to give birth in the city. Iona's mother did not share these superstitions, and Iona admitted that the soul of a warrior who was killed three hundred years ago lives in it.

Brother and sister are very close: as a child, they ran away from home, once ran away from the castle in the May rain and, according to Iona, then for the first time “understood the First Winter”. Erwin called her the only person who understood him. Iona dreamed of becoming an artist and painting icons and frescoes.

In "Arrow, Coin, Spark"

In the spring of 1774, Iona was married to the Earl of Vittor Shayland, grandson of a merchant and banker (see the Wedding of Iona and Vittor). The wedding took place in the first winter in March. Brother Iona admitted that he was happy to leave, but did not like her husband: he seemed to her a funny creature to which you can get used. To collect the bride price, Vittor secretly sold the Light Sphere through Harmon's merchant (see Sale of the Light Sphere). (Radiant Sphere; Sale of the Radiant Sphere)

Erwin saw his sister like this: a fragile figure "of white porcelain", moving anxious lips, dark eyes, like rolled up by a haze, the feathers of parrots, woven into tar hair, and a snow shawl. In Waymar, a feast in honor of Harmon Ion was stopped by the beating of Joaquin Yves Hannah, who was overthrown by the knights of the count. (Joaquin Eve Hannah) She checked whether his jaws were intact, and chided him: there is no need to fight for the girl, and the death of people is not fun. According to her, after leaving the North, she had not seen a single death for a month and was happy about it. Joaquin remembered her condescension as humiliation. Harmon, hiding from the satellites the true purpose of the deal, explained that the count collects money for his wife: Lady Iona allegedly wanted to open a hospital for the maimed and sick. On June 2, 1774, Iona and her husband were at a summer ball in Faunterra: Vittor introduced her to Mira, who posed as Gloria Northwood, already as Countess Shayland, and the emperor congratulated the couple on their wedding. When asked by Mira if she missed the first winter, Iona ambiguously replied: “Just like at noon I miss my own shadow.”

Erwin, who left with an exploit in the Beyond, sent a letter to his sister in Shayland on four sheets before the long-distance crossing. Meanwhile, the Duke of Desmond was struck by a stone disease. Fearing the rebellion of the Flemings and Baron White, Lady Sophia summoned Iona and her husband to the First Winter: the Kairs adored the Northern Princess, and she was as much a symbol of the North as a bat with an arrow. Here, in late August 1774, Iona was the first to meet Erwin, who had returned from the Beyond. She waited for him at sleepless nights, feeling that trouble had happened to her brother, and ran to him barefoot, in a nightgown. In her father's bedroom, Iona and her husband were present when Erwin spoke of the Lodge of Dara and of the soldiers in scarlet shirts serving "Lord Adrian", and when Desmond called his son the reigning Duke. During this scene, she stood at her brother's right shoulder.

“My good brother has never drawn a blade in my honor, and I am so grateful to him for it!”

In "Only One Star"

When Erwin rebelled against the emperor, Iona was in the First Winter. (Northern Uprising) Treasurer Robert Origin told Erwin the size of the ransom: twenty thousand ephes Shayland paid immediately and pledged to pay ten thousand annually for another ten years, a total of one hundred and twenty thousand. Of the first money received, 2200 hilts went on the wedding, while Iona took one and a half thousand to Shayland to distribute to the poor and to hospitals.

Only Sister Erwin revealed the true intent of the ultimatum. He told her to leave, but she refused. Iona admitted that while he was in the Beyond, she was standing on the tower and thought of throwing herself down, and that she was “tired of death.” She reminded her brother that she was an Origin and he was her lord, and demanded to order her anything but to leave: to seek money, allies, command the army.

Iona visited prisoner Mark in prison: in a scarlet silk dress, with a feather of the same color in her hair, she brought him a jug of wine and a vase of fruit, but she could not let him go. By her order, Mark began to feed from the soldier's kitchen and every three days to examine the doctor. Iona said that one day, wanting to understand what it was like to have her grandmother Lady Jessica held hostage by Reis, she herself asked her father to lock her in prison for two weeks. She assured Mark that the war would be short, and offered him, when the Origins took Faunterra, to serve as Erwin's head of the secret guard.

On September 10, 1774, the last day before the campaign, Erwin at the table at all announced that he wanted to see his sister and Vittor in Waymar. At night Iona came to her brother and admitted that the count had already dedicated her to their common plan with Erwin. The main role, according to her, she played: she had to make sure that her husband did what he had to do. Erwin gave her forty swords: "If Vittor upsets you..." “He’s not — he’s — he’s laughing! Waymar is yours." When Erwin admitted that he was afraid, Iona slapped him and reminded him of his father's words: "Peace is a nightmare, and war will be more fun." The next day, she and her husband left for Waymar in a circular way: by carriage to the northern port, by sea to the Preforest and further along the river. There, Iona actually led the county policy: persuaded Craig Northwood to bring the Northwood army to his brother's aid and compiled an appeal to the Great Houses by the Origins. (House Northwood)

In Waymar, Mira was kept: her Vittor was taken from Ulyana Monastery. Mira dined with Iona, her companion Jane, and Cyre Seymour Steel. Iona wondered with her on the maps on the night of the near moon. When Mira, investigating the disappearance of Lindsay's servant, started talking about secret moves and accused the count, she was put in a cell in the lower circle of the dungeon. (Lindsey) Later, Iona confessed to Father David that it was with this injustice that the chain of her mistakes began. She then read Mira's letter, found a secret passage on the castle circuit, and, with Seymour Steel's detachment, intercepted the Emperor's men on the night road, who were taking Mira, Jane, and the bound Martin Shayland. Seeing Mira's bruises and Jane's wounds, Iona took Jane and the Dew. She told Mira that she owed her, and offered her the choice of either becoming her guest in Waymar or leaving. Mira left and said goodbye to Iona the best enemy that the gods could create. Iona replied to her:

“I am not your enemy.”

"A Doll on the Throne"

Waymar and the way to the capital

In December 1774, the Kairs opened barrels in Waymar's dungeon, where about thirty corpses lay, of Martin's victims. Martin pleaded to let him go and called his potion an "imperfect elixir" prolonging his youth. I didn't kill Iona's brother. She locked him in the lower circle of the dungeon, and she kept a glass of the "elixir of immortality" and kept it in a box with a crow's feather from Mira's diary. She later explained that she owed Mira two lives, her own and Jane's.

When news of the defeat of the Northmen at Pixie came, Iona felt at a distance the death of six thousand compatriots, but felt that Erwin, Robert and Damon were alive. Vittor then sent troops to help Adrian, and after Erwin's victory, he immediately wrote to him. Iona suspected her husband, but did not check him with an elixir, although Seymour offered to pour a potion to the count.

In early 1775, Iona left Waymar for the capital, where his brother celebrated the victory. Vittor did not go with her: he referred to the cases and the anger of the empress, who sent a pigeon with a demand to extradite Martin to court. In Labelin, Erwin's new vassalage, Iona met her parents, who, with a hundred of the most loyal warriors, were also on their way to Faunterra. They included Jemis Lilliday and Crown Raven Mark, whom Iona had previously visited in prison. He said that through the object captured in the Beyond, he managed to talk to the owner of the Rings, and Lady Sophia asked him to heal her father in exchange for this object. The rail road was destroyed, and the Origins rode, and then made a hook east through Izluchina and Niar. The entire month's journey from Waymar Ion saw mass graves at Pixie, ruined villages and flocks of crows. She was met by Alanis, now the mayor of the capital. Iona asked her what the war had cost her, and Alanis replied, "Illusion." Erwin chastised his sister for her suspicions against Vittor: he needed an alliance with the Shaylands. Her brother broke her crow feather with the words that there are no pure victories, and Iona interpreted the sign as a "crowd victory", which pleases only scavengers. Mira rebuked Iona by saying that Martin was alive and contained in the Ivy Tower, but Iona referred to the duty of his wife and sister.

Faunterra

Erwin showed his sister the wasteland on the slope of Hanoi, where he conceived to build the Cathedral of Agatha the Radiant with the grotto of Kosuli and the gallery of northern heroes. (Roe Deer Grotto) Iona was worried about his vanity and spending. She helped rebuild the Palace of Pen and Sword: invented the windows in the full height of the ballroom, the fountain “Tears of Emilia” and the blue silk “waterfall” behind the throne of the small hall. She then secretly poured Martin's pot into her dying father's cup, and Desmond began to recover. Later, he moved his hands and spoke.

When the Infirmary, sent by the Puppeteer, came to the palace and touched Desmond with the Object, Iona felt that the "path of death" around her father had retreated, and wanted the Infirmary to be allowed to come again. (The Healer) Her father ordered her to be seized at the gate, and Iona took Erwin's word not to meet with "this brat." A year ago, among the vassals there were painful rumors for Iona that Desmond would deprive Erwin of his inheritance and give the dukedom to her. With Hector's arrival, Ion was found by her brother to have intercepted letters of Southern defeat in Litland addressed to Minerva. (Hector of Shimmery)

Contrary to the plan of her brother, who wanted to grab the Znaharka at the gate, Iona, along with Alanis, secretly met her at the summer theater. Iona slashed her arm with a kair dagger, and Znaharka covered the wound with an Object for a diamond. Alanis asked for her scar to be removed, but then Jemise's men showed up, and Znaharka fled. She was killed at the Northwood camp, and Craig claimed the body and the Item. Erwin screamed at his sister, but then he forgave. When Znaharka's Hand was recovered, Iona and his family tried to get her to work. (Healer's Hand) The item responded only in the hands of Gwenda, Erwin and Luis, a captured mechanic whom Iona persuaded to put on the Hand. (Louis Maria)

Iona reproached his brother for cruelty and callousness. At the military council before the battle with the Snowdrops, she begged the Kairs not to kill the hungry peasants and told Erwin that Richard was standing in front of her, and Erwin was missing. Then his brother led her in a secret move and revealed his plan to her: his idle life was a pretense and a trap for the Puppeteer, and his sister was given the role of a "critic", according to whose doubts he checked his game. There was a kiss between them, after which they both realized that they would not be happier. Erwin promised after his sister from Waymar returned a walk under the most beautiful downpour, and she took from him a promise to spare the peasants. After receiving a seven-page letter from Vittor, where the count admitted that he was insufferably bored, Iona burst into tears and decided to return to her husband. On the way she met Joaquin, remembered their Waymar meeting, and later, suspecting him a servant of the Puppeteer, took him prisoner.

In The Voice of Winter

In the interlude "Winter's Voice" Iona appears briefly: she giggles in her brother's ear as he flaunts himself in front of the court ladies with his exercises with a new sword. (Voice of Winter) Erwin notes that neither she nor Alanis were aware of his failures in the fencing room.

The “Yanmei Hunt”

Return to Waymar

From Faunterra, Iona rode with the kairs for three days to Leixiti, and from there sailed along Smoky Distance, carrying prisoner Joaquin with her. At each stop, she politely asked him, “Who is the Puppeteer?” He was perfectly fed, the kairs addressed him only to "you", and two attempts to escape, one of them in Leixiti, failed. Iona knew he loved Alanis. In retaliation, Joaquin told her that Vittor had instructed Harmon to secretly sell the Light Sphere, and that he had delivered Alanis' letter to Earl Arrowback, after which Adrian had died, and that Erwin knew about the letter, though he was against it. (Radiant Sphere) Iona did not believe and was crying.

On 5 May 1775, Iona returned to Waymar. She was tormented by the question of who she was now: the owner of the castle, Origin or the Countess Shayland. At lunch, Martin, whom Vittor had freed and called "healed", sat to the left of the count, and Iona to the right. Vittor explained that he sold the Sphere for their love: the Duke of Desmond allegedly asked for an “unworldly” ransom of one hundred thousand ephesas. Robert, on the other hand, called Erwin another sum, a hundred and twenty thousand. Iona refused to read her husband’s letter, because according to the northern custom, deeds of honor are decided in words, not on paper. She ordered Joaquin to be released with an apology, because for the second time she arrested the innocent, to monitor Martin and find the doctor who treated him.

Vittor confided in his wife and explained to her his correspondence with the ruler of the Sunset Coast: through the sunsets, he hoped to attract the Shavans of Moran of the Steppe Fire, dissatisfied with the departure from Litland. Iona advised not to spend money and rely on the power of the First Winter. Iona decided to become a better wife and reflected on three types of love: Miriam, Sophia and Emilia. The latter, the kinship of souls, she fully experienced only to Erwin. The brother who asked the pigeon about the Sphere, she replied with a short tape: “I am ashamed to say, but I do not dare to lie...” She presented the deal as a sacrifice for her happiness. Doctor Galuers told her that Martin's illness is rooted in fear of death, strong men, and the Dark Ido.

Investigation

Having received advice from David’s father not to take the letters in hand, Iona told the Cairams to open them with gloves and read aloud. (Father David) With Kair Irving, she investigated the story of a Waymar prison prisoner who escaped in 1769, killing two jailers. The former jailer Lard said that Kilmer and High had been “working” for years, and on the eve of his escape, he hissed at him: “It’s sad for you.” Iona found out that the old Count Vincent Shayland had died a week after the escape, when Vittor, according to the priest, was in the church.

Soon Nexia Flame and her brother Somerset arrived in Waymar. Nexia at night told Iona about her love for Erwin, and Iona promised to be her "thread" to her brother. That same night, Seymour, sent "extremely cautiously" to apprehend Joaquin, massacred the inn and killed several townspeople. Iona cut off the strip from his bloody cape, stripped him of his position as captain of the guard, handed over command to Irving, and threatened to take the cape for any new harm to civilians. Vittor then kicked Seymour out, grabbed his wife by the hair, and threw her, "You're a lollipop. “Northern shit.” Iona apologized and admitted that she had told her brother about the Sphere.

In negotiations with Abbot Hosch, Benedict Fleming's envoy, Iona demanded public penance from the rebellious Count in Faunterra and was angry that her husband had invited the ambassador without her knowledge. After Nexia went naked for breakfast, Iona suspected poisoning. The barber Harry Hog, who brought a note from Vittor, had her lick the paper. (Harry Hogg) Old Count Elias Northwood showed her a model of a ship with a spark generator and shared his guesses about the prisoner.

Conjecture and Coup

Iona understood how the Puppeteer works: as an archer, he first shoots, and kills with the second shot. Letters with Ulyanina Dust forced Manson to kill the emperor, and the book forced Nexia to go naked. (Ulyana's Dust) To Kyra Irving, she stated her conclusions: the prisoner did not leave the castle, Kilmer and High probably broke his wall on orders, Vittor lied as if he had not seen the prisoner, and the old count died of terror after seeing something come out of the secret passage. Iona sent Irving with a ring-print to Erwin, ordered two pigeons to be sent and reported that the Puppeteer was Vittor, and Nexia was probably carrying a trap to the capital. She herself remained, saying that she was an Origin and a North. Later, when she was leading the sunset Hash Eilish to the prisoner’s cell, she came out and said to her, “Your husband is a happy man.”

On May 27, 1775, Iona staged a coup in Waymar. Vittor ordered the Northerners to sail into the First Winter at night, and Iona submissively gave a kair Brandon a collection order. In the evening she killed the castellan Harold with a knife, piercing his throat right through the sheet with the list of supplies. She then poured oil on the donjon's staircase and set it on fire, cutting off her husband on the fourth floor. Iona hung on Captain Leus' hand as if begging to save her husband, and killed him with a spark dagger discharge, and Seymour stabbed his aide-de-camp. Stevens' eight-kire captured the tar tower, and the burning resin broke the garrison of three hundred soldiers into small groups. Iona had forty northerners. Before the fight, she confessed to Seymour that when she was afraid, she sang to herself a lullaby “Star, come up, look in the eye...”.

Under the fire of Finger of Wilhelm, from which barber Harry Hog fired, Iona alone walked through the fireballs to the reserve phalanx, singing a lullaby. (Wilhelm's Fingers) Her dress is smoldering. When the soldier threw a spear at her and the kair wanted to kill him, she stopped the kair and spared the spearman. She's disbanding the phalanx. Harry Hogue shot Stephens' kire, but the dying barber still managed to shoot under Joaquin's direction: he burned Seymour through and killed several more northerners. Iona then surrendered to be released by the thirteen remaining soldiers.

In "Humans and Gods"

Plen

Vittor broke his word and ordered the Northerners to shoot after, and Martin dropped a spark net, "net", on them from the gate tower. Iona was shot with an arrow below his knee, and she stabbed herself under his left chest. The knife left in the wound did not allow it to bleed out immediately. Vittor healed her with the Object and, as he later said, "infused" primrose into her. (Firstblood) He needed a valuable hostage, and the sunsets he wanted to show his strength. Erwin and the whole empire thought Iona was dead. Vittor showed the town elders his wife chained to a bed in the burned-out bedroom and promised to burn her alive in front of the Duke if he was "ignorant".

Martin put a large dog cage in the bedroom with two pairs of keys, he and Joaquin, who became her jailer. Martin splashed burning oil on her foot and forced Joaquin to hit the captive. Iona warned Joaquin that all who remained in the cursed castle would perish, and advised him to flee without looking back. When Vittor spoke to Erwin through the moon bracelet, Iona managed to shout to her brother:

Erwin, don't think about me. Kill the monsters!”

That's how Erwin found out her sister was alive. On June 9, Ice arrived in Waymar, and in it Iona recognized Richard's brother, whom the family mourned. Richard accused her of trying to kill him, and Iona swore that he did not understand anything. He beat Joaquin for beating the "sister of the northern lord" without demand, and then let him beat her further. With the help of Ulyanina Dust, Iona was forced to rewrite with her own hand a false confession of incestuous connection with Erwin and conspiracy against Richard, with all the family signs of authenticity. The forgery didn't fool Erwin's doppelganger at Waymar port. After the failure at the port, Vittor gave Richard the key to Iona's bedroom, which had previously been kept by Joaquin, and instructed him to bring the captive to the wall as a shield against the Kairs.

The Shadow of the Great Tree

Hostage

In the summer of 1775, Desmond's troops besieged Waymar. Every morning, the bound Iona with a bag on his head was taken out of the gate to show his father's kiram that she was alive, and Desmond paid for it with a cart of grain. Even without seeing anything, she described to the northerners the famine in the castle and called the number of the Rings in the garrison. On the wall of the house, the North posted a sign “Only with Iona.”

When the prisoner Alanis was brought to Waymar, she condemned Iona’s “treason” to her husband, but secretly remained her friend. On the night of August 2, a stranger dressed as a sentinel was killed at Iona's door, and in the afternoon of August 2, the alarm rose: "Iona is trying to escape." On the same day, she stood next to a friend in the chapel, where Alanis struck Paul and Vittor. Later, Iona recalled that Alanis took her hand, confessed her love and died. Joaquin later found Iona broken: "You couldn't have done otherwise. And I couldn't." On the march, the Chosen One's army across Northwood, Iona was carried in a cage with the sign "She betrayed her husband." (Vittor Shayland) She depicted madness and submission, but remembered the commands that are controlled by the Rings, and gave signs of her own. Before the night attack of the Northwoods and Kiers, she silently knocked on the rods "We are going to the West." In the fight, she pounced on the cart that had squeezed Joaquin, broke his ribs, and injured him and Martin with a sharpened bone. However, the ambush was Richard's trap, and Craig Northwood died.

For the first time in a month, Iona spoke to Martin, calling him “the master”: she said that the elixir of immortality does not exist and immortality gives the Absolute. Martin, who had been searching for an elixir for years, left shocked. He soon strangled Laura Farway in a drunken form and blamed Iona's "sorcery".

Leed

In Leed, who surrendered to Richard without a fight, Iona was kept in a cage in the basement of the Lillydeev castle arsenal. Gwenda, hired as a nanny for Wittor's children, secretly came to see her. Iona broke the iron rod of the cage with his bare hands, knocked out Martin's teeth and crushed his palm, and Gwende, the bearer of the firstblood, ordered to kill the guard and burn the barrels. Paul called Gwenda a "squirrel", killed her with a blow to the chest, took her Perst and returned Iona to the cage.

In late November 1775, Erwin and Hyder Leed and Aubrey entered the castle during the assault on Leed by the Shavans and found her sister alive. Martin caught them with Perst and made Iona bark and lick his hand. Then she showed him the forearm on which the command "Take the Perst, give it to me" was written by Dust Gwenda, and Martin gave the Perst. Iona fell down the corridor behind them, burned the courtyard where the enemies had settled, and killed Baron Dorcaster. She almost burned everyone who was in the yard, and stopped only after the words of her brother: “Sister, enough.” Martin was running through a hole in the wall of a burnt out needy. After her escape, Iona shaved her hair bare, "like Captain Theobart," and said that she would no longer want to wear feathers. Erwin, who was suffering from pneumonia, wanted to leave his sister with Aubrey in Leed, and hurry to the First Winter, until Martin informed Vittore about the escape of the captive. Iona refused to obey and said that her place as a bearer of Perst was on the battlefield, and her brother had to take her with him. By a small detachment with Hyder Leed, the Kairs, the Leed townspeople, and the jokers from the Lillydean stock, they galloped east in the footsteps of Paul's Shavans. On the way, Iona told her brother about the six months of captivity: “I tried to kill myself, but Vittor returned. That’s why he gave me the firstblood.” At night, in a herding hut, she watered her freezing brother with her blood.

Battle for First Winter

On December 2, 1775, in the Battle of the First Winter, Iona first fired on the Shayland convoy with the Perst, and then lay among the corpses in a field invisible to the enemy, and killed the Shavans-peppers, clearing the way for his brother. (Battle for First Winter) In the evening, she healed the seriously wounded Erwin with the Hand of the Inkling, never having used it before. First, she gained experience on the hopeless wounded: eight healed, three killed. Along the way, she cured her brother's pneumonia. In preparation for this, she prepared a dagger in case of failure and sang herself the same lullaby. In the morning she was going to go to the wounded: the doctor said that three hundred and twenty people would die.

After the death of her father, Iona did not remove the Hand of the Znaharka, but returned to the infirmary and worked without rest: she closed the mortal wound for twenty, about fifty people a day. Erwin did not leave her, so that the wounded would not tear his sister to pieces. She did not take off her Hand, even when Adrian threatened through the Voice of God to destroy the Origin Items with a deconstructor. Soon Minerva brought Nathaniel to the infirmary with a broken skull, which was found near an underground lake. Iona healed him, and then anxiously told Mira: realizing what would live, Navi asked: “Why?”

That same night, Richard broke into Erwin's room and started a "game" with Perst. Iona tried to persuade him to return to his family, but he found her gesture when she took her brother by the hand, proof of their connection. In front of her, Richard killed Captain Gordon Sue and his father. When Erwin stunned his brother with the sparkle discharge of Winter's Voice, Iona took off Richard's Belt and Perst: Objects obeyed the primrose in her veins. (Voice of Winter (Sword)) She asked Erwin to kill him, reminding him of his father's body, and he did.

After the victory

Erwin and Minerva forbade Iona to "see his tragedy" and gave a light wig, and Minerva, touching the Eternal Hilt, gave her the right to be a "tragic victim" for one hour a day. (Minerva) Upon learning that Adrian had frozen Vittor in the Womb, Iona first presented her husband's cruelest executions, but then decided that his fate should be decided by the supreme court, not her revenge.

On December 3, her mother, Lady Sophia, returned from a long voyage with Princess Darkwater Mireille. After learning from Mireille about her mother's plan to give the Objects to each person, Iona took off her headscarf and said that she would always be ashamed of her initiation: from people with the Objects she saw nothing but cruelty, and she herself became a beast by wearing a Perst. Of the fifty known carriers of the firstblood, according to her, only one was a “ray”, and the rest were monsters. Together with Erwin and Minerva, she declared herself an opponent of the new Tree.

“Yes, I have absolutely everything in me. Unlimited love - to the full sacrifice of oneself, to humiliation, to death. And equally endless is cruelty.”

In negotiations with the delegation of Adrian Ion secretly kept under the shawl of the Perst, although her brother forbade her to wear it, and felt from Lady-in-the-Darkness the "aura of murder". (Lady in the Dark) When Robert turned his neck to the old queen, Iona nearly opened fire on the other ambassadors. Erwin held her and at Adrian's request removed the Perst from her hand. She begged not to reveal the "cursed secret" of the Star. When Nathaniel offered Minerva a choice, Iona asked him to kill him because he wanted to.

In "Fantasies"

In Fantasia, which the author calls possible futures, Iona lives in the First Winter. (Fantasies) Erwin calls her Countess Shayland, the empress's prima vassal. Her personal bodyguard is kair Aubrey.

Repentance

Shortly after the war, Iona locked herself in the mountain. She was visited by King Francis-Ilianus: he told about the prophetic dreams that nine years ago foreshadowed even the “wooden structure” of her Gun, and advised to confess to the impartial confessor, the capital of the higher mothers, and accept strict penance, but first visit Minerva. (Francis-Ilian; The Weapon) Iona did exactly what she said. Her penitential letter of eight pages was the key for the Church to restore its authority: the clergy imposed a harsh penance on the princess and demanded repentance from all the finger-bearers. Iona spent six months in penitential wandering and saw thousands of poor people. On March 17, 1776, on her birthday, she became convinced that the Hand of Znaharka did not cure black leprosy.

Summer of 1776

In the summer, Iona returned “dark, ascetic, roasting like a lynx.” She did not give in to her mother, refused treats “when people die”, and hid knives and crossbows in the room. Lessons with the Power Gauntlet from Minerva failed: the stones from her touch flew up. (Glove of Might) Later, when the kairs asked her to raise the bones of the drowned woman from the bottom of the lake, she forgot to untangle the Glove rays from the harpsichord, which had just been raised on the shooting range, and threw it into the lake.

One hot night, Iona appeared to Vittor, though he was frozen in the Womb. She shot him with a crossbow, and he disappeared. Iona was then afraid to sleep alone and slept in her brother's room until he decided what she had dreamed. At the divination with her mother and Minerva, she said that she often sees the ghosts of scoundrels, and every full moon Alanis calls the spirit, but she never came.

Mercy Clinic

When Iona returned, she immediately took up the hospital. In the Mercy Clinic, which ten years ago was founded by her mother as a shelter for the sick old and poor, she brought order in one day: patients were sorted into heavy and light, the heavy were taken first. Iona took thirty-two patients a day, treated for free and did not wear a mask, although she required masks from kairs. Minerva conceived to turn medicine into an exact science and told her only to recognize diseases so that doctors would study without the Subject, but she did not dare to take the Hand of the Znacharka. Then Iona at night "ghost" treated patients in hotels around the clinic, lulling them with a touch. There was a rumor that Agatha heals herself, and feathers with pillows were bought out. The friends quarreled, and then reconciled, and Minerva offered Iona to become Minister of Health.

The last one in the castle, Iona, learned that Erwin was Minerva's secret favorite for about a month. She knew his fiancée Demeter from boarding school: a third of the course became fans of the southern woman, and Iona and Alanis had to team up "to put her in her place." Jemis joked that Leed Castle had been renamed Black because Iona had "repainted it" with the Perst. Erwin recalled that during the war, her sister killed a hundred Shavans. In "The Composition on the Theme", the schoolgirl writes an essay about how the stern Northern Princess heals the wounded knight with a touch of her hand: for ordinary people, Iona became the heroine of fairy tales.

Personality and Appearance

Iona is fragile, thin, tall and black-haired. She has dark, “smoke-covered” eyes and very moving lips. Before captivity, she weaved the feathers of parrots into her hair; after Leed, she remained shaved and wore a light wig. She eats almost nothing, loves bitter chocolate, writes poetry and draws. Iona is mystical and believes in signs: in mare's suit, in crow's feather, in cards. She is characterized by almost supernatural sensitivity: she feels the pain and death of loved ones even from afar and feels the mood of people around. She never lies and demands from herself strict loyalty to the commandments. Northern education gave her coolness and military training: she knows by the name of each of her soldiers and gives orders, "like a matry sergeant." Iona herself confesses that she has everything in her: boundless love, up to the sacrifice of herself, and equally boundless cruelty. She is characterized by sacrifice and a tendency to commit suicide; her brother and Minerva directly reproached her for being used to being a victim.

Relationships

Erwin

The closest person she loves the most and with whom she has, in her words, “Emilian” love, a kinship of souls. Their relationship sometimes goes beyond the fraternal: in the “A Doll on the Throne” they kissed and refused it themselves. Erwin rescued her from Leed, and she healed him after the battle.

Vittor Shayland

Husband. Marriage without love was replaced by sincere attempts to love, then suspicion, rebellion and half-year captivity. Vittor called her "soul", but kept her in a dog cage. After his imprisonment in the Womb, Iona refused to avenge herself and demanded a trial.

Martin Shayland

Dever, executioner and jailer. Iona gave him fear. She kept him alive in 1774, and he bullied her in captivity and in Leed tried to get her dead.

Richard

The older brother she mourned. Returning to Ice, he considered her a traitor and Erwin's mistress. Iona tried to return him to the end, but after the death of her father she asked him to kill.

Alanis Almera

A friend of the board. In Waymar Alanis condemned Iona for appearances, and before her death, in memory of Iona, she took her hand and confessed her love. In Fantasies, Iona considers her dead and calls her spirit in vain, but in The Composition on the Theme, Alanis is apparently alive under the name of Mrs. Gale, a rural teacher: wearing black gloves, with a cane, maimed, nicknamed by the children "gargoyles" (see Alanis Almera).

Minerva

First a prisoner and a rival, later a close friend. Iona thought she owed Mira two lives, and in 1774 released her.

Joaquin Eve Hannah

Iona twice touched his pride and once arrested him innocent, and he became her jailer and beat her in captivity.

Captain of her guards. Iona pardoned him for the massacre in the inn, but before the coup, she trusted him again. Seymour died in Waymar defending her.
